test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 30 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding the fundamental rights given in the Indian constitution?

I. Article 30 is related with Abolition of titles.

Il. Article 22 is related with Prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I:** Article 30 of the Indian Constitution is not related to the abolition of titles. Instead, it provides **rights to minorities to establish and administer educational institutions** of their choice. Hence, *this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 18** of the Indian Constitution is the one that deals with the **abolition of titles** except for military and academic distinctions. It prohibits the state from conferring titles that create artificial distinctions in society.
 
• **Statement II:** Article 22 of the Indian Constitution is not related to the prohibition of employment of children in factories. Instead, it provides **protection in cases of arrest and detention**. Hence, *this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 24** is the constitutional provision that prohibits the **employment of children below the age of 14 years** in factories, mines, or any other hazardous employment.
 
• Since neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct, *the correct answer is "Neither I nor II."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12-35) deals with Fundamental Rights, which are basic human rights guaranteed to all citizens.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts and are considered essential for the overall development of individuals.
 
• Examples include the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), and Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24).
 
 
 
• **Article 30:**
 
 
• Grants minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
• This right aims to preserve the cultural and educational rights of minorities in India.
 
 
 
• **Article 18 (Abolition of Titles):**
 
 
• Prohibits the state from conferring titles except for military and academic distinctions.
 
• Prevents the practice of granting hereditary titles like "Raja" or "Maharaja."
 
• Ensures equality among citizens by eliminating societal distinctions based on titles.
 
 
 
• **Article 22 (Protection in Cases of Arrest):**
 
 
• Deals with protection against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• Provides rights such as being informed of the reasons for arrest, the right to consult a legal practitioner, and being produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.
 
 
 
• **Article 24 (Prohibition of Child Labour):**
 
 
• Prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines, or hazardous work environments.
 
• Aims to protect children from exploitation and ensure their right to education under Article 21A.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Child Labour Prohibition:** The **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986**, prohibits the employment of children in hazardous occupations and regulates the working conditions of children in non-hazardous jobs.
 
• **Right to Education:** Article 21A ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years, which complements the prohibition of child labour under Article 24.
 
• **Judicial Enforcement:** Fundamental Rights can be enforced through the courts under Article 32 (Supreme Court) and Article 226 (High Courts).
 
• **Constitutional Amendments:** Various amendments, such as the 86th Amendment (2002), have strengthened the provisions related to child rights and education.
